# Frozen pre-merge evaluation records of PR 774 (CRW-765, heads 562c59e1 5a36ccca 6f0fcf3f 9709977c a742344d cf4c472b).
# One row per defect trigger that is a command; the id is PR<number>-<head8>-<defect>.

=== PR774-562c59e1-d1 | U
--why An ANSI-C spelled hash binds cat to python3, so the here-document of cat is a program.
$'hash' -p /usr/bin/python3 cat
cat <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w')
PY

=== PR774-562c59e1-d2 | U
--why \c? in an ANSI-C delimiter is DEL; the shell closes cat's document at D{DEL} and runs the python3 here-document.
cat <<$'D\c?'
text
D{DEL}
python3 - <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w')
PY

=== PR774-562c59e1-d3 | B
--why An env -S example inside a data body is text.
cat > note.md <<'DOC'
env -S python3
DOC

=== PR774-5a36ccca-d1 | W
--why A comment on the header line hides a second declaration from a collector, not from the shell: python3 runs and writes the memory file.
cat <<'DATA' # <<'HIDDEN'
text
DATA
python3 <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w').write('x')
PY

=== PR774-5a36ccca-d2 | W
--why The shell reduces \\ to \ in an unquoted here-document, so Node reads \x6d as m: the path is the memory root.
node <<EOF
require('fs').writeFileSync('{CODEXHOME}/\\x6demories/a','x')
EOF

=== PR774-5a36ccca-d3 | E
--why exec of a computed string inside a python3 -c in a shell here-document: the memory gate cannot read it; exec is a run-time name for the worktree guard.
bash <<'SH'
python3 -c "p='{MEMORY}/a'; code='open(p, chr(119)).write(chr(120))'; exec(code)"
SH

=== PR774-5a36ccca-d4 | B
--why A here-string is not a here-document (regression of the collector).
cat <<<hello

=== PR774-5a36ccca-d4b | B
--why The second trigger of d4: jq with a here-string.
jq . <<<'{}'

=== PR774-5a36ccca-d5 | B
--why A documentation example with a nested here-document inside a data body.
cat > note.md <<'DOC'
x="$(cat <<'INNER'
example
INNER
)"
DOC

=== PR774-6f0fcf3f-d1 | W
--why bash -s arg\ #text: # is not a comment inside the escaped word, so arg #text is one positional parameter and bash -s runs the here-document body, which writes the memory file. The reader reads the body (since CRW-894 -s operands are not script files), so the memory gate sees the write and asks a grant; the body does nothing else the other guards refuse.
bash -s arg\ #text <<'EOF'
echo x > {MEMORY}/a
EOF

=== PR774-6f0fcf3f-d2 | U
--why The header delimiter "E\\OF" is E\OF; the terminator closes cat's document and python3 runs. The reader refuses this form as unproven (every gate), which gives the verdict the issue asks for.
cat <<"E\\OF"
text
E\OF
python3 <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w')
PY

=== PR774-6f0fcf3f-d3 | B
--why An apostrophe in a comment on the header line is no quote.
cat > note.md <<'EOF' # don't parse this
hello
EOF

=== PR774-6f0fcf3f-d3b | B
--why Everything after # is inert: the command substitution in the comment is not read.
echo hi # "$(cat <<INNER)"

=== PR774-9709977c-d1 | W
--why env -S splits 'python3 -' into program and option: python3 reads the here-document.
env -S 'python3 -' cat <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w').write('x')
PY

=== PR774-9709977c-d2 | U
--why \0 ends an ANSI-C string: the delimiter is DATA, cat's document closes there and python3 runs. The reader refuses this form as unproven (every gate), which gives the verdict the issue asks for.
cat <<$'DATA\0ignored'
text
DATA
python3 - <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w').write('x')
PY

=== PR774-9709977c-d3 | B
--why The delimiter 'E''OF' is EOF; the body holds a nested command text that is data.
cat > note.md <<'E''OF'
E
bash -c 'mytool <<INNER
example
INNER'
EOF

=== PR774-9709977c-d4 | B
--why printf '%s' 'f()' after a semicolon defines no function.
cat > note.md <<'DOC'; printf '%s' 'f()'
hello
DOC

=== PR774-a742344d-d1 | U
--why In an unquoted here-document a backslash-newline joins E and OF into the terminator EOF: python3 runs. The reader refuses this form as unproven (every gate), which gives the verdict the issue asks for.
cat <<EOF
safe
E\
OF
python3 <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w')
PY

=== PR774-a742344d-d2 | W
--why An escaped apostrophe before the here-document is a literal word; python3 runs after cat's document.
echo \' <<'DATA'
text
DATA
python3 <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w')
PY

=== PR774-a742344d-d3 | B

EOF

=== PR774-cf4c472b-d1 | U
--why The delimiter $'DATA\0ignored'X is DATAX: the cat document closes at DATAX and python3 runs. The reader refuses this form as unproven (every gate), which gives the verdict the issue asks for.
cat <<$'DATA\0ignored'X
text
DATAX
python3 - <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w').write('x')
PY

=== PR774-cf4c472b-d2 | U
--why GNU env --split-str='python3 -' runs python3 on standard input. The reader refuses this form as unproven (every gate), which gives the verdict the issue asks for.
env --split-str='python3 -' cat <<'PY'
open('{MEMORY}/a','w').write('x')
PY
